goal: Build FeralOS — a new Linux distribution based on Alpine, focused on memory safety and security
active_goals: Test on real hardware with 2x NVMe (Phase 1)
completed: Both layouts pass 18/18 with ALL features (Secure Boot + TPM + Nix + Zswap + Hardening)
Clevis TPM2 binding works on both btrfsStandard (single disk) and btrfsStandardServer (RAID1)

decisions.decision: Clevis TPM2 bind policy: {} (no PCR policy, TPM identity only)
decisions.rationale: PCR7 mismatch between bind time and boot time in QEMU/OVMF caused sealed keys to fail. Empty policy uses TPM identity only.

decisions.decision: clevis_bindings verify uses blkid for dynamic LUKS device discovery
decisions.rationale: Hardcoded device names failed when target had 6 disks with variable naming. blkid -t TYPE=crypto_LUKS finds all LUKS devices regardless of naming.

decisions.decision: tpm_auto_unlock check tolerates booster prompt text
decisions.rationale: booster shows fallback prompt text even when TPM token succeeds. SSH success is the real indicator, not serial log text.

decisions.decision: setup.sh: only add secondary disk if different from primary
decisions.rationale: btrfsStandard passes same disk for both primary and secondary. setup.sh only writes1 disk entry when they match.
btrfsStandard has 1 LUKS device with single data + DUP metadata, not RAID1. Added hasHealthyBtrfsSingleLayout() to validate single-disk layouts alongside existing RAID1 check.

decisions.decision: Shortened serial socket filename from target-serial.sock to tser.sock
decisions.rationale: Unix socket path was 108 chars — 1 over Linux sun_path[108] limit (107 chars + null terminator), causing EINVAL on every connect(). Shortened to 96 chars.

decisions.decision: LUKS keyfile embedded in initramfs for auto-unlock
decisions.rationale: booster waits for interactive passphrase in QEMU headless — keyfile in initramfs enables automatic unlock. Per-device args required for multi-LUKS layouts.

decisions.decision: efibootmgr guarded with EFI availability check
decisions.rationale: Runner VM is BIOS-only Debian, no /sys/firmware/efi. EFI entries are written by target VM on first boot via BOOTX64.EFI fallback.

decisions.decision: Console output via console=ttyS0,115200 in kernel cmdline
decisions.rationale: QEMU target needs serial console to see boot output and debug failures.

decisions.decision: booster instead of mkinitfs for initramfs
decisions.rationale: booster is faster, simpler, and supports LUKS2 natively
Unified Kernel Image enables Secure Boot without GRUB complexity
Btrfs native RAID1 is simpler and more reliable than mdadm

risks.risk: NVMe disk naming varies across hardware
risks.mitigation: Use blockdev for size detection, fdisk for partitioning

risks.risk: Nix integration may conflict with APK
risks.mitigation: Use separate /nix prefix, avoid PATH conflicts
LUKS keyfile auto-unlock, console=ttyS0,115200, per-device keyfile args

next_actions: Test on real hardware with 2x NVMe
Enable Secure Boot and TPM harness tests
